title: Shapley meets Rawls: an integrated framework for measuring and explaining unfairness
abstract: arXiv:2603.26476v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Explainability and fairness have mainly been considered separately, with recent exceptions trying the explain the sources of unfairness. This paper shows that the Shapley value can be used to both define and explain unfairness, under standard group fairness criteria. This offers an integrated framework to estimate and derive inference on unfairness as-well-as the features that contribute to it. Our framework can also be extended from Shapley values to the family of Efficient-Symmetric-Linear (ESL) values, some of which offer more robust definitions of fairness, and shorter computation times. An illustration is run on the Census Income dataset from the UCI Machine Learning Repository. Our approach shows that ``Age", ``Number of hours" and ``Marital status" generate gender unfairness, using shorter computation time than traditional Bootstrap tests.

translated_title: Shapley遇上Rawls：一个度量与解释不公平性的集成框架
translated_abstract: 可解释性与公平性通常被分开研究，近期的少数研究才尝试解释不公平性的来源。本文表明，在标准的群体公平性准则下，Shapley值可以同时用于定义和解释不公平性。这为估计不公平性、对其进行统计推断，以及识别导致不公平性的特征提供了一个集成框架。我们的框架还可以从Shapley值扩展到高效-对称-线性（ESL）值家族，其中一些方法提供了更稳健的公平性定义和更短的计算时间。我们在UCI机器学习库的Census Income数据集上进行了实证演示。我们的方法表明，“年龄”、“每周工作小时数”和“婚姻状况”是造成性别不公平的因素，且计算时间比传统的Bootstrap检验更短。
tldr: 本文提出利用Shapley值及其扩展的ESL值家族，将群体不公平性的定义、度量和解释整合到统一框架中，并在Census Income数据集上识别出年龄、每周工作小时数和婚姻状况是造成性别不公平的关键因素，同时计算效率优于传统Bootstrap检验。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an integrated framework using Shapley values and their ESL extensions to jointly define, measure, and explain group unfairness, identifying Age, Hours per week, and Marital status as key drivers of gender unfairness on the Census Income dataset with faster computation than traditional Bootstrap tests.
